properties.statement:
A RUN THAT PROVED EVERYTHING THE PROJECT OWNS AND WAS BLOCKED ELSEWHERE HAS NO HONEST STATUS. Reported by the qs project 2026-09-04: 'An acceptance run that proved everything qs is responsible for but could not exercise one plan (blocked by the simulator) had to be either `passing` or `blocked`. I chose `passing` with a long findings paragraph; THE STATUS ALONE MISLEADS EITHER WAY.'

CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: `verify.rs:152` documents the set as `planned` / `passing` / `failing` / `skipped` / `blocked`. There is no `partial`.

⭐ WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A MISSING ENUM VARIANT, and why it belongs beside the prose findings on this same day: THE STATUS IS THE FIELD EVERY ROLLUP READS AND THE FINDINGS ARE THE FIELD ONLY A HUMAN READS. `loop_status.verifications` counts by status; `coverage_report` and the unproven-capability gap key on `passing`. So a run recorded `passing` with a paragraph explaining it was partly blocked is COUNTED AS PROOF by every computation in the system, and the qualification reaches nobody. They chose the option that overstates because the option that understates would have read as a failure that never happened.

THIS IS THE SAME AXIS AS `fact:defect-a-status-can-advance-past-its-own-prose-and-nothing-says-so`, from the other direction: there the prose went stale behind a status; here the prose carries a truth the status cannot express. In both, the machine-read field and the human-read field disagree and nothing joins them.

THEIR SUGGESTION, offered as an either/or: a `partial` status, OR per-clause findings so a check can pass for the part under the project's control and be blocked elsewhere.

⚠️ AND `partial` WOULD OWE EVERY READER A RULING, which is the real cost and the reason this is recorded rather than built. Does a `partial` check satisfy `verified`? Does it clear the unproven-capability gap? Does `coverage_report` count it? A new status is not a new word, it is a new answer that eight computations have to give. Adding it without settling those would produce exactly the silent miscount it is meant to prevent.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how often this shape occurs. n=1, on a project whose acceptance layer depends on an external simulator — which may be the general case for anything tested against hardware or a shared test bed, or may be peculiar to it.

SECOND SIGHTING, 2026-09-25, recorded by the 2026-09-28 triage. dev_storyflow (storyflow #654) reported a live walk that ended 31/35, where the 4 "failures" were the intended tightening, proved by a parity check. Their words: "`passing` overstates that and `failing` misreports it, and there is nowhere to say 'passing, with 4 expected-change assertions' … a list view shows only the status." It is a different shape from qs's (an EXPECTED CHANGE, not a blockage) with the same cause, re-measured on 0.72.0. The enum is still planned/passing/failing/skipped/blocked/superseded. loop_status counts the run as a plain pass and leaves it out of `attention`, and scan_nodes brief shows the status alone. n is now 2, across two projects. Root cause: fact:root-cause-a-run-has-one-status-and-its-qualification-reaches-no-rollup-2026-09-28. The open question the 2026-09-06 change said "remains the open idea it was" now has a Decision node: dec:idea-a-run-can-pass-with-its-exceptions-stated.
